articles.title: Barriers to recruitment in paediatric orthopaedic surgical trials : a qualitative study embedded in the Big BOSS trial.
articles.authors: Kirton JA, Achten J, Young B, Perry DC, Cherry MG
articles.study_type: Qualitative study nested within a randomized controlled trial
articles.population: Consultant surgeons at NHS sites involved in the Big BOSS trial for slipped capital femoral epiphysis
articles.outcomes: Barriers to recruitment identified through semistructured interviews, analysed thematically
articles.take_home: Recruitment to the Big BOSS trial failed because of multiple interconnected problems: too few eligible patients, unclear eligibility criteria, surgeons' confidence in their preferred treatments, lack of research support, and patients' concerns about surgery. The study shows that understanding these challenges through qualitative research can help design better surgical trials in future.

articles.title: Consensus guidelines in the management of paediatric flexible flatfoot : a Delphi study of the British Society of Children's Orthopaedic Surgery.
articles.authors: Morrow EM, Bennet S, Morrison SC, Bridgens A, Mavrotas J, Brousil J, et al.
articles.population: Consultant orthopaedic surgeons, registrars, fellows, allied health professionals and advanced nurse practitioners from the British Society for Children's Orthopaedic Surgery
articles.sample_size: 169 in Round One and 167 in Round Two
articles.outcomes: 26 consensus statements on assessment and management of flexible flatfoot in children, with 24 statements reaching the 75% consensus threshold
articles.take_home: UK orthopaedic experts have agreed on 26 guidelines for assessing and treating flexible flatfoot in children, though there remains uncertainty about which specific surgical procedures to use. This consensus provides a framework for consistent management across the country.

articles.title: Supervised physiotherapeutic scoliosis-specific exercises provide limited additional benefit at 24 months in braced adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis: a randomized trial.
articles.authors: Zhang X, Liang M, Huang Y, Lin B, Lin Y, Yang Y, et al.
articles.population: Adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis undergoing brace treatment
articles.outcomes: Change in spinal curve angle (Cobb angle) and health-related quality of life at 24 months
articles.take_home: Supervised physiotherapy exercises reduced spinal curvature slightly more than self-directed exercise, but the difference was too small to matter clinically. Quality of life improved similarly in both groups.

articles.title: Hip-related tenotomy and progression to severe displacement of the hip in nonambulant children with cerebral palsy : a nationwide cohort study.
articles.authors: Bakhtiyar M, Iljazi A, Wong C, Petersen MM, Balslev-Clausen A
articles.population: Nonambulant children with cerebral palsy (GMFCS level IV or V) with established hip displacement enrolled in Danish Cerebral Palsy Follow-Up Program
articles.outcomes: Severe hip outcome defined as migration percentage of 50% or more, or hip osteotomy surgery
articles.take_home: Children who had a hip-related tenotomy were less likely to develop severe hip problems over ten years compared to those who did not have the procedure, particularly those with less severe movement limitation. However, in children with the most severe movement limitation, hip problems still progressed significantly even after the procedure, suggesting careful selection of which children might benefit is important.

articles.title: Prone positioning and high-frequency oscillatory ventilation in early paediatric acute respiratory distress syndrome (PROSpect): an international, two-by-two factorial, response-adaptive, phase 3, randomised controlled trial.
articles.authors: Curley MAQ, Kneyber MCJ, Cheifetz IM, Kong M, Mahapatra S, Schwarz AJ, et al.
articles.study_type: International two-by-two factorial randomised controlled trial
articles.population: Children aged 2 weeks to 20 years with early moderate-to-severe acute respiratory distress syndrome requiring mechanical ventilation for less than 96 hours
articles.sample_size: 424 children randomised across four groups (126 supine-conventional, 130 prone-conventional, 90 supine-HFOV, 78 prone-HFOV)
articles.outcomes: Primary outcome: ventilator-free days up to day 28. Secondary outcomes: mortality at day 28, airway obstruction, pressure injuries, and haemodynamic instability
articles.take_home: Neither prone positioning nor high-frequency oscillatory ventilation improved the number of days children could breathe without a ventilator compared to standard care. Prone positioning carried a higher risk of airway blockage and pressure injuries, whilst high-frequency oscillatory ventilation was associated with more episodes of unstable blood pressure.

articles.title: Proximal Fibular Epiphysiodesis or Resection May Alter Lower Limb Alignment in Growing Children.
articles.authors: Poynter L, White S, Walker JL
articles.population: Children with below-knee amputations undergoing proximal fibular epiphysiodesis or resection
articles.outcomes: Changes in medial proximal tibial angle, anatomic distal femoral angle, and proximal fibular height at minimum 2-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Proximal fibular surgery in growing children often reduces fibular head prominence but may cause the shin bone to tilt outward (valgus), sometimes excessively, so children need regular monitoring after surgery for changes in leg alignment.

articles.title: Four large language models in parent-oriented education for pediatric flexible flatfoot: Quality, readability, hallucination, and reproducibility.
articles.authors: Servet E, Unat B, Bilgin MA, Karabulut C, Gonder N
articles.study_type: Cross-sectional comparative content analysis of AI-generated text
articles.population: Parent-oriented questions about paediatric flexible flatfoot submitted to four large language model chatbots
articles.sample_size: 20 parent-oriented questions submitted in triplicate to four models, generating 240 responses
articles.outcomes: Readability indices, clinical quality scores (Mika grade, PEMAT-P, DISCERN, QUEST), hallucination assessment, reproducibility of responses, inter-rater agreement
articles.take_home: None of the four chatbots (ChatGPT, Claude, DeepSeek, Gemini) met recommended readability standards for parents, and their responses were only moderately reproducible when given identical questions. Choosing a chatbot should be based on readability and usefulness rather than presumed accuracy, with any information checked by a clinician first.

articles.title: Association between cemented and uncemented cups and risk of revision in patients aged 65 years or older following primary total hip arthroplasty: a study of 310,515 patients from the Nordic Arthroplasty Register Association.
articles.authors: Latifi R, Kornvig S, Mohaddes M, Ali M, Kristensen TB, Hallan G, et al.
articles.population: Patients aged 65 years or older undergoing primary total hip arthroplasty for osteoarthritis or childhood hip disorder sequelae
articles.outcomes: All-cause acetabular cup revision rates at 0-1 year, 1-6 years, and 6-26 years follow-up
articles.take_home: Cemented cups had a lower revision risk in the first year after hip replacement surgery, but a higher revision risk over longer term follow-up (6-26 years). In patients aged 80 years or older, there was no clear difference between cemented and uncemented cups after the first year.

articles.title: Radiologic Results of Selective Thoracic Fusion in Adolescent Idiopathic Scoliosis (AIS) Lenke Type 3 and 4.
articles.authors: Alkharsawi M, Trobisch PD, Frank J, Pishnamaz MeD M
articles.population: Adolescents with Lenke type 3 or 4 idiopathic scoliosis undergoing selective thoracic fusion
articles.outcomes: Thoracic and lumbar curve magnitude, coronal and sagittal balance, lumbar lordosis, and revision surgery rates at immediate postoperative and 1-year follow-up
articles.take_home: Selective thoracic fusion in carefully chosen adolescents with certain types of scoliosis showed that the unfused lower spine curve improved spontaneously over the first year after surgery. Initial imbalance and loss of lower back curve reversed by one year, though one patient needed revision surgery.

articles.title: Tractionless Hip Arthroscopy in Children With Suspected Septic Arthritis of the Hip: A Comparative Cohort Study.
articles.authors: Jamnik AA, Wilkens CR, Tareen NG, Jo CH, Wilson PL, Ellis HB, et al.
articles.population: Children with suspected septic arthritis of the hip requiring operative treatment
articles.sample_size: 164 children (34 treated with tractionless hip arthroscopy, 130 with arthrotomy)
articles.outcomes: Operative time, hospital length of stay, repeat surgery, emergency department return, hospital readmission, postoperative sequelae, C-reactive protein change, and postoperative pain medication use
articles.take_home: Tractionless hip arthroscopy appears to be a feasible alternative to open surgery for children with suspected septic hip infection, with similar rates of complications and repeat surgery. Children treated with arthroscopy may have better inflammation markers and lower pain medication requirements, but the study cannot confirm it is as safe or effective long-term as traditional surgery.

articles.title: Measurement of Femoral Neck Anteversion Angle in Children With Intoeing Gait by Using Femoral Plain Radiographs: A Retrospective Observational Study.
articles.authors: Liu MY, Yao SH, Liaw CK, Wang JH, Lin CH, Chen CH
articles.population: Children aged 5 to 12 years with intoeing gait
articles.outcomes: Agreement between femoral neck anteversion angle measurements using plain radiography versus CT scan
articles.take_home: Plain radiographs using a standardised method measured femoral anteversion very similarly to CT scans, with only a small 1-degree difference that is unlikely to matter clinically. This suggests plain radiographs could be a useful alternative to CT for assessing intoeing gait in children, avoiding unnecessary radiation exposure.
